author: Gmelin, 1788

art.subject: Lesser Coucal (Centropus bengalensis), adult in breeding plumage: head, neck, underparts and tail black with a dull gloss; wings chestnut, the flight feathers tipped dusky; pale buff shaft streaks often visible on the scapulars and wing coverts; tail long and broad, black. Bill black, thick and arched; eye dark; legs dark grey, with a long straight hind claw.
art.pose: clambering in tall grass with the tail half-cocked, side view
art.scene: Tall grass and reed edge on a southern Korean island in late spring, warm light; no people, buildings or text
art.build: Medium-sized, slim-bodied ground cuckoo, clearly smaller than Greater Coucal and about the length of a Feral Pigeon including the long tail; short rounded wings and a long, broad, graduated tail often held half-cocked. Bill stout, arched, shorter than the head. Legs long and strong for a cuckoo, with two toes forward and two back. Skulks and clambers in tall grass; flight short, heavy and floppy.
avoid: Do not paint a bright red iris (Greater Coucal, Centropus sinensis).
Do not paint a short tail; it is long, broad and graduated.
Do not give the adult a slim, straight bill; the bill is thick and arched.
Do not paint chestnut on the head or underparts.
